```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(stockplotr)
```

Integrated assessment models such as FIMS and Stock Synthesis are fit to
many data sources at once, including landings and fishery and survey
indices of abundance. {stockplotr} has a set of diagnostic plots for these
fits that work the same way for each model. They are based on the figures
from [r4ss](https://github.com/r4ss/r4ss) and on diagnostics from
[JABBA](https://github.com/jabbamodel/JABBA) and
[ss3diags](https://github.com/PIFSCstockassessments/ss3diags).

| Diagnostic | Function | What it shows | Equivalent in other packages |
|------|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Index fit | `plot_index_fit()` | Observed indices with intervals and the expected index | r4ss: `SSplotIndices()` subplots 2 and 5 |
| Landings fit | `plot_landings_fit()` | Observed and expected landings | r4ss: `SSplotCatch()` |

## Input data

Each function takes the output of a model directly:

- **FIMS**: the output of `FIMS::get_estimates()` (on its own or passed
  through `convert_output()`), or the `FIMSFit` object itself. FIMS reports
  years as indices (1 = first model year), so use `start_year` to label the
  x-axis with years.
- **Stock Synthesis**: the output of `convert_output()`, or the list returned
  by `r4ss::SS_output()`.
- **Other models**: the output of `convert_output()`, or a tidy data frame
  (see `?prepare_fit_data`).

Indices and landings are first reshaped with `prepare_fit_data()`, which
returns the observed and expected values, the observation error, and the
residuals. Call it directly to inspect the data behind any of the plots:

```{r}
fits <- prepare_fit_data(example_data)
head(fits)
```

The examples below use the Stock Synthesis model in `example_data`. The same
calls work for FIMS; for example, with the FIMS example model:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
data("estimates_big_optimized", package = "FIMS")
fims <- estimates_big_optimized
plot_index_fit(fims, start_year = 2001)
```

Each plot can be saved with a caption and alternative text that describe
the data and options used to make it, with `make_rda = TRUE` (see
`vignette("how-caps-alttext-are-made")`).

## Fits to indices and landings

```{r}
plot_index_fit(example_data)
plot_index_fit(example_data, log = TRUE)
```

Indices with lognormal errors are often easier to judge on a log scale,
where the intervals are symmetric.

Landings are usually fit closely; large residuals indicate a problem.

```{r}
plot_landings_fit(example_data)
```
